Definition: a clatter, i.e. (abstractly) whirring (of wings); (concretely) a cricket; also a harpoon (as rattling), a cymbal (as clanging)
BiblicalUsage: tsᵉlâtsal is the word for a clatter; a cymbal, a cricket, a harpoon. It appears 5 times in Scripture, including 2 Samuel 6:5 and Psalms 150:5.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God gave us tsᵉlâtsal because the idea it carries belongs in His Word.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
